evidence_scope_projection.definition: Overall prostate cancer evidence, excluding estimates solely about aggressive prostate cancer. General estimates from papers that also report aggressive endpoints remain included. Uncertain endpoints retain their existing review and pooling restrictions.

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 3 studies yielded an overall effect size of 1.06 (95% CI: 1.01–1.11), suggesting that glucosamine is associated with a higher risk of prostate cancer\aggressive. These findings were supported by low between-study heterogeneity (I² = 0.00%), indicating consistent findings across the included studies.

disease_scope_review.reason: The HR of 1.07 is explicitly reported for incident prostate cancer generally, without an aggressive subtype definition.
